FieldShift AI: Physics-Guided Crop Rotation & Soil Resilience Engine
FieldShift_AI_NASA_Space_Apps
FieldShift AI is an interactive agro-climatic decision-support web application developed by Team Ultimate_Void for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data). Smallholder farmers in semi-arid and climate-vulnerable regions, such as Pakistan’s Lower Indus Basin, are trapped in water-intensive monocultures (Wheat–Cotton) that degrade soil health and leave fields barren during the 60-day summer bare-soil window (April–June) under extreme heat. FieldShift solves this by harmonizing 120 months (2016–2025) of NASA Earth observations (NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM, MODIS NDVI, ECOSTRESS LST, SRTM) with a Monotonically Constrained XGBoost machine learning model and deterministic FAO-56/Maas-Hoffman biophysical physics. The engine evaluates and compares three multi-season crop rotation strategies side-by-side in English, Urdu, and Sindhi. It quantifies exact irrigation water savings, natural legume nitrogen fixation (+2.5 to +5.3 bags of 50kg Urea fertilizer saved per acre), and net economic returns (~PKR 157k–170k/acre), providing a transparent Satellite Fusion Confidence score and Ground-Verification Checklist to support local farmer judgment.
Git Hub repository : (https://github.com/Mubashir-Uddin-AI/FieldShift.git)

1. What It Does & How It WorksFieldShift AI is a physics-guided agro-climatic decision-support web application that helps farmers transition from water-heavy, soil-depleting monocultures (such as Wheat–Cotton) to climate-resilient crop rotations.Workflow: When a user selects a farming zone (e.g., in Sindh's Lower Indus Basin) or inputs custom coordinates, the backend fetches and harmonizes 120 monthly observations (2016–2025) via live REST APIs across six NASA missions (NASA POWER, SMAP, GPM/IMERG, MODIS NDVI, ECOSTRESS LST, and SRTM).The AI & Physics Brain: It combines a Deseasonalized LinearRegression trend analyzer (isolating multi-year warming and drying slopes) with a Monotonically Constrained XGBoost Regressor (monotone_constraints=(1,1,-1,-1,-1,1)). This strict mathematical constraint guarantees the machine learning model never violates physical laws (e.g., higher temperature and solar radiation always increase stress; higher moisture reduces it).Biophysical Guardrails: Predictions are anchored by FAO-56 evapotranspiration ($ET_c = ET_0 \times K_c$), Maas-Hoffman electrical conductivity ($EC_e$ dS/m) salinity yield-loss physics, and a localized PKR/Urea conversion ledger. The tool automatically detects April–June bare-field vulnerability windows (NDVI < 0.25) and ranks three multi-season crop rotation strategies side-by-side.2. Benefits & Intended ImpactEconomic & Ecological Benefits: Replaces the 60-day summer bare fallow with short-duration nitrogen-fixing legumes (Mungbean or Sesbania) and deep-rooted oilseeds. This reduces irrigation water demand by up to 53% to 60%, fixes natural nitrogen equivalent to +2.5 to +5.3 bags of 50kg Urea fertilizer saved per acre (~PKR 11,500/acre in input cost savings), protects topsoil microbes from thermal sterilization, and secures resilient net returns (PKR 157,415 to 170,220 per acre).Intended Impact: To empower smallholder farmers, agricultural extension workers, and rural financial institutions in Pakistan and global semi-arid basins to make data-driven, de-risked planting decisions that ensure long-term soil health, food security, and water conservation.3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software UsedProgramming Languages & Frameworks: Python 3, Streamlit (minimalist editorial UI), Plotly (interactive telemetry charts & horizontal bar comparators), Folium & streamlit-folium (geospatial mapping with Esri World Imagery and CartoDB Positron layers).Machine Learning & Data Stack: xgboost (XGBRegressor with monotonic constraints), scikit-learn (LinearRegression), pandas, numpy, requests.APIs & Data Sources: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API, NASA SMAP Surface & Root-Zone Soil Moisture, NASA GPM/IMERG Precipitation, NASA MODIS NDVI Vegetation Indices, NASA ECOSTRESS Land Surface Temp, NASA SRTM Elevation, and ESA Sentinel-2 / ERA5 via Open-Meteo.Development & Collaboration Tools: Git, GitHub ([https://github.com/Mubashir-Uddin-AI/FieldShift.git](https://github.com/Mubashir-Uddin-AI/FieldShift.git)), and Google Gemini / Antigravity IDE (utilized for coding assistance and documentation formatting, with all biophysical formulas independently verified by Team Ultimate_Void).4. How the Project Is CreativeZero-Hallucination Hybrid AI: Unlike standard black-box LLMs or unconstrained neural networks that can hallucinate fake crop yields or anti-physical trends, FieldShift uses Monotonic XGBoost fused directly with classical agronomic equations (FAO-56 and Maas-Hoffman).Minimalist Editorial UX: It departs from cluttered, overwhelming technical dashboards by adopting a high-contrast editorial interface (#F6F4EF warm paper background, #285C4D forest green, and #A84F36 terracotta accents) that delivers complex satellite intelligence into plain language with localized multi-language support (English, Urdu اردو, and Sindhi سنڌي).5. Key Factors Considered by Our TeamSmallholder Economic Realities: We recognized that a farmer cannot adopt a pure "cover crop" that yields zero income. Therefore, our model prioritizes marketable legumes and oilseeds (Mungbean, Chickpea, Sunflower, Guar) that simultaneously fix nitrogen and sell for cash in local mandis.Satellite Limitations & Blind Spots: Recognizing that 9km SMAP pixels and coarse satellite grids cannot see sub-acre canal seepage or subsoil salinity, we integrated a quantitative Satellite Fusion Confidence Score (74%) and an explicit Ground-Verification Checklist (prompting soil lab tests, tube-well EC checks, and canal Warabandi schedule reviews) to ensure technology supports—rather than replaces—local human expertise.
